argument_macro_structure.dominant_argument_form: Modus tollens and thought experiment-based reasoning
argument_macro_structure.premise_explicitness: Mostly implicit, with key premises stated informally (e.g., 'subjective experience can be dissociated from objective time')

argumentative_quality.dialectical_reasonableness: Moderate: acknowledges objections (backwards causation, fatalism) but relies on logical possibility rather than empirical plausibility
argumentative_quality.logical_relevance: High: all thought experiments directly support the thesis that subjective time does not uniquely determine objective becoming
argumentative_quality.premise_acceptability: Mixed: some premises (e.g., that memory ordering can be reversed) are empirically grounded, others (e.g., backwards causation) are stipulated as logically possible

distinctions_drawn: Growing Block vs. Backwards Block vs. Diminishing Block
explicit_definitions_given: Subjective past: memory hierarchy at a moment
Subjective future: state toward which one feels headed based on memory
Objective past: states that already exist or have come into being
Objective future: states not yet come into existence

dialectical_engagement.objection_handling: Acknowledges objections (backwards causation, fatalism, memory of future) and responds by appealing to logical possibility, statistical mechanics, and the stipulation of the thought experiments
objections_raised: Backwards causation seems impossible (Dummett's apple example)
Memories of the future but not the past are strange

method_and_evidence.evidence_type: Thought experiments, empirical examples (déjà vu, waking from sleep), conceptual analysis

philosophical_orientation.sentiment: Neutral, exploratory; aims to break down intuitions rather than defend a specific theory
philosophical_orientation.thematic_focus: Temporal becoming, subjective experience of time, ontology of time

structural_organization.structure_type: Sectioned essay with numbered sections (I–V) and subsections (a, b)

summary_of_core_decisions: The paper argues that the subjective experience of time does not uniquely determine the objective structure of temporal becoming. It introduces two alternative models (Backwards Block and Diminishing Block) and uses thought experiments to show that subjects in those worlds would have the same subjective experience as we do under the Growing Block model. The conclusion is that our intuitions about time are not reliable guides to its metaphysics, and empirical investigation is needed.

thesis_commitment.conclusion_type: Moderate: argues for the possibility that non-intuitive models of becoming could produce the same subjective experience, thereby undermining the intuitive privilege of Growing Block
